messages:
maria-support: Heads up — customer SUP-12345 reporting a spike of 5xxs from the Hosted API for ~2 hours. They see quota/rate-limiter errors but responses are 500/502 instead of 429. Customer traffic dropped and they escalated.

maria-support: Quick paste from customer logs:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota-service: upstream timeout",
  "code": 500
}
```
They attached 20+ traces showing same pattern — quota check call to internal quota-orchestrator times out and the gateway classifies as 5xx.

maria-support: Severity is customer P1 (production impact). They want reproduction steps and ETA. Adding @alyssa-eng-sre and @tim.backend for triage.

tim.backend: reading traces now. I can see gateway -> quota-orchestrator -> identity-kv and one of the identity calls hit a socket_timeout. The quota-orch does not translate dependency timeout to a 4xx; gateway sees the fail and surfaces a 5xx. Suspect faulty error-mapping in quota-orch middleware.

tim.backend: snippet from trace service (trace id abc123):
```
quota-orch: POST /check -> timeout after 1500ms to identity-kv
quota-orch: raised QuotaServiceError(code=E_DEP_TIMEOUT)
gateway: mapped exception to 502 when quota response missing
```

ben.platform: if quota-orch returns anything non-4xx the gateway treats as upstream error. We should have quota-orch return a deterministic 4xx (429/403) on quota denial and return 504 only when upstream timed out — but crucially gateway should translate E_DEP_TIMEOUT -> 503 or 504 and the client should treat as retryable or show explanatory 429? hmm.

alyssa-eng-sre: this is a reliability bug — two paths:
- short-term mitigation: route traffic for the affected customer to fallback quota service that returns proper 429s (we have fallback pool: quota-readonly). Can we switch customer to fallback while we patch?
- medium-term: fix error classification in quota-orch and add circuit-breaker to identity-kv with faster failover.

sarah.ops: I created INC-4829 in ops and applied the emergency runbook. Repro steps for engineering:
1) curl request above (use customer's api key)
2) capture gateway logs with `tail -n 500 /var/log/gateway/gateway.log | grep <customer_key>`
3) fetch quota-orch logs: `kubectl logs deployment/quota-orch -n infra --since=10m | grep trace:abc123`
4) show the quota-orch stacktrace (attached in ticket)

quota-bot: ALERT: quota-orch latency spike detected — 5xx rate 18% over baseline. AlertID QO-2026-0315-01

deploy-bot: Deploy noticed: quota-orch v2.4.1 rolled at 1828876000 by ben.platform — rolling restart 6h ago.

tim.backend: that deploy included a new identity-kv client that changed socket timeouts from 300ms -> 1500ms (oops). That explains the sudden upstream timeout pattern. Reverting timeout may reduce occurrences but we still need proper error mapping.

ben.platform: plan:
- immediate: revert identity-kv timeout to 300ms in quota-orch config (will do a canary patch)
- immediate: add gateway rule to map quota-orch E_DEP_TIMEOUT -> 429 when quota decision missing? alternatively, map quota-orch timeouts to 503 so clients can retry. Need product input on UX.
- follow-up: add integration test that simulates identity-kv timeout and asserts gateway returns 429/4xx for quota-denied flows.

alyssa-eng-sre: I'll take on monitoring + incident blameless postmortem. Also we'll add circuit-breaker with fast-fail (fail after 2 slow calls) on identity-kv.

sarah.ops: mitigation executed: routed SUP-12345 traffic to quota-readonly fallback at 1828881030. Customer confirmed reduced failures but noted slightly higher latency. (reacts :white_check_mark:)

maria-support: customer updated at 1828881100 — "Errors dropped from ~18% to 1%, thanks. Will watch for a day." They requested ETA for full fix.

tim.backend: canary revert patch queued — `kubectl set env deployment/quota-orch IDENTITY_KV_TIMEOUT=300 -n infra --record` then monitor. I'll rollout canary to 10% first.

ben.platform: added gateway mapping PR: map QuotaServiceTimeout -> 503 with explanatory body (we can iterate to 429 if product decides). PR: github.com/redwood/quota-orch/pull/412

alyssa-eng-sre: also adding a synthetic test to our canary checks: call generate with a stubbed identity-kv slow response and assert gateway returns 503 within 2s. Will schedule for tomorrow.

sarah.ops: ops note: increased quota-orch HPA target from 3->6 to absorb short term burst at 1828881200. CPU upscaling happened automatically.

maria-support: Customer asked about billing — they saw invoices but worried about retry storms. We told them we will not retroactively bill for throttled calls; CC finance on follow-up.

ben.platform: created follow-up tasks:
- QO-215: error mapping fix (target 3d)
- QO-216: identity-kv circuit-breaker + timeout tests (target 5d)
- QO-217: gateway-level defensive mapping for quota-orch timeouts (target 2d)

maria-support: confirming next steps: canary revert + HPA increase + reroute to fallback completed. Will keep customer posted and close once no regression for 24h.

deploy-bot: Canary patch applied to quota-orch (10%): deploy-id dpl-7783 at 1828881285

tim.backend: canary looks healthy so far. still seeing a couple of 502s in the last 5m but much reduced. continuing to watch.

alyssa-eng-sre: logging follow-up: add `quota_reason` field to gateway logs to make classification obvious. Filing SRE-98.

maria-support: adding final note to ticket INC-4829 and marking the customer notified. Thanks all. (reacts :pray:)

sarah.ops: closing incident thread here, moving to postmortem when engineering tasks land.
